pr_body:
Added support to read/write flash on stm32h743.

Tested on a nucleo_h743zi with samples/drivers/flash_shell.

Fixes #29831
pr_comments:
Please notice that MCUBoot is not support due to the minimum flash write size over 8 bytes.
https://github.com/mcu-tools/mcuboot/issues/713

> Please notice that MCUBoot is not support due to the minimum flash write size over 8 bytes.
> [mcu-tools/mcuboot#713](https://github.com/mcu-tools/mcuboot/issues/713)

Indeed, after publishing my PR, I tried to play with MCUBoot, and noticed that the swap would fail. As far as I could test, I did not notice any issues while playing around with flash_shell sample.

Hi, thanks for your thorough review.

> I would advise to create a dedicated stm32h7 driver (ie not based on flash_stm32.c).

I thought about it initially but I was afraid to have a lot of copy/paste from flash_stm32.c, so I decided to go with with the approach used for flash_stm32wbx.c: using ifdef to remove functions definitions from flash_stm32.c and defining them into flash_stm32wbx.c.
The downside is the multiple ifdef popping arround in flash_stm32.c
If that is not acceptable I'll see how i can improve it, maybe splitting flash_stm32.c into flash_stm32_cmn.c and flash_stm32_v2.c ? (there is already a v1).

Otherwise I've addressed the various suggestions you've made, and hopefully fixed the buildkite/zephyr.

I noticed an issue when using samples/drivers/flash_shell/, if i try to `flash write_pattern 0x20000 256` twice, on next reset I see the content which has been erased but the pattern is not there anymore. If you have any idea let me know.

Do you want me to update the PR with the commits I made to address your suggestions or shall I wait to have the issue above fixed ?

Thanks

> I thought about it initially but I was afraid to have a lot of copy/paste from flash_stm32.c, so I decided to go with with the approach used for flash_stm32wbx.c: using ifdef to remove functions definitions from flash_stm32.c and defining them into flash_stm32wbx.c.
The downside is the multiple ifdef popping arround in flash_stm32.c
If that is not acceptable I'll see how i can improve it, maybe splitting flash_stm32.c into flash_stm32_cmn.c and flash_stm32_v2.c ? (there is already a v1).

If we consider the fact that H7 flash driver might require in the end to support simultaneous operations to 2 banks, I think that we'll end up hacking a lot flash_stm32.c file and I'd prefer to avoid this situation. 
Also, I don't think splitting flash_stm32.c would be that great (flash_stm32_v1.c is used together with flash_stm32.c for F0, F1, F3 and L0), it is a different split as you're proposing for v2.
So in the end, the simplest is to opt for a monolithic flash_stm32_h7.c (this might require some file renaming to minimize confusion with other stm32 flash dirvers, but I'll take care of that part).

> One point I'm not sure is that if we should consider writing unaligned blocks. I think as a first version it would be better to reject as done on other drivers, unless there is a good reason to do so.

Since the flash words are pretty larges (32 bytes), I thought it was relevant, I don't mind removing it.

> Since the flash words are pretty larges (32 bytes), I thought it was relevant, I don't mind removing it.

This is a fair point, but I'm not sure that upper layers are able to deal with this, While I'm sure they're able to deal with various write bloc sizes (this is why we provide a `flash_parameters.write_block_size `). Anyway, if this appear to be possible and requested, it could be added later. Let's start with a safe implementation.

@erwango, I have addressed your suggested changes, except for [this one](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/30043#discussion_r530468924).

Thanks for your review.

>     * add the minimum flash descriptions in dtsi files for available H7 SoCs

I'm not sure to understand exactly what that means. Is it related to the write-block-size/erase-block-size properties ?

> I'm not sure to understand exactly what that means. Is it related to the write-block-size/erase-block-size properties ?

Yes!
Latest push should have fixed the buildkite/zephyr. Sorry about that...
@nicovince would you mind rebasing to fix CI issue ?

> @nicovince would you mind rebasing to fix CI issue ?

Done.
@nicovince reopen?

> @nicovince reopen?

I'm still trying to figure out why the CI built successfully when I finalized this PR and why it failed later...
I'm pretty new to zephyr development, what shoud i do ? 
Repoen #29831 and create a new PR, or continue on this one ?
Reopen this time means submit another PR.

> I'm still trying to figure out why the CI built successfully when I finalized this PR and why it failed later...

@nicovince, there is a trick indeed.
My understanding of what happened is the following: 
In CI, only a limited subset of platforms vs samples/tests are build. On top of that a specific run is launched for each impacted board (based on path board/foor/bar).
On daily builds, all test/samples vs platforms combinations are run. And I guess this is where the _m4 targets builds were launched.

By the way, I'm looking at the issue.
Definition of flash controller on H7 M4 cores have some consequences that should be checked.
I'm not sure exactly how this should be fixed.
I propose to push a new PR with your commits when I'm done

@erwango, I was getting to the same conclusion.

I started modifying the dtsi in order to take into account the different flash address based on the core (0x800_0000 for m7, 0x810_0000 for the m4), and the dts compilation passes, but another failure rises at linking stage regarding the cache invalidation call (SCB_).
Setting that call under ifdnef CORE_CM4 does the trick...
Is there an invalidate cache call on M4 cores ?

> Is there an invalidate cache call on M4 cores ?

No. No flash cache mgmt on H7 M4 cores it seems. 
Anyway, there are few more hickups on the M4 core flash driver support.
So I ended up thinking that flash driver support on M4 core should be disabled cleanly for now on.

Hi, I ve some questions:

- Is for M4 core a flash-drviver support foreseen? When?
- what is necessary to do in order to adapt M7 driver to make it running with M4?

Thank you in advance for any answer.

comments:
@nicovince 

> Am I missing something or is flash operations not supported yet on Zephyr OS for stm32h7 devices ?

Indeed this is not supported yet

> and the drivers/flash/flash_stm32.c seems to reference old regmap layout.

flash_stm32.c is the common stm32 flash layer. To have a working flash driver, it requires an additional soc specific `flash_stm32h7x.c` driver that will provide h7 specifics.

> I'm fairly new to Zephyr OS and I'm willing to give a try at adding support for this if no one else is working on it. 

This would be welcome. I would advise to study a bit the H7 flash layout, see if this is close to one of the other series supported and build from there. A handy sample to test your work is `samples/drivers/flash_shell`.

review_comments: I'm also confused here. Why length to be used in SCB_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr would be different from len?

Same issue as above.
Although I suspect there is still a bug lying somewhere because if I do a write_pattern with a length of 256 at offset 0, then a write_pattern of length 32 at offset 0, I still see the data at offet 32 to 63.

Ok, I saw that as well.
I would tend to say this is related to a bug in upper layers since this cannot be seen if `flash erase` is run manually between two `flash write_pattern`

Are you sure ?
I want to wait while QW bit is set in either of the bank, not both of them simultaneously.
My bad, this is fine indeed.

I'm a bit puzzled by this line given that get_sector(offset) = offset / FLASH_SECTOR_SIZE.
A subtlety I didn't catch maybe?

I noticed an issue when playing around with `zephyr/samples/drivers/flash_shell/`:

If i write a few bytes at the beginning of a sector, then do a `flash write_pattern` at an address further away in that sector, I would still see the few bytes written at the beginning of the sector even though `write_pattern` performs an erase on the sector.

So, with this line I'm telling the driver I want to invalidate the cache at the first address of the sector which has been erased.

I think you will face the same issue I have on STM32G4 #30231
There may be some discontinuity between bank1 and bank2 on some chip, when dual bank, with smaller flash .
Ex: stm32h747zi has 2M flash but stm32h747IG has only 1M flash, in this case real number of sector will be smaller, and by the way you cannot rely on FLASH_SECTOR_SIZE which is defined to 8 for all soc STM32H747xx.

I've had a look at files under `modules/hal/stm32/stm32cube/stm32h7xx/soc`, and all SOCs defining `DUAL_BANK` have a 1MB `FLASH_BANK_SIZE` (based on the comments).
So as far as I understand it the h7 family would not be impacted by this fragmented issue. What do you think ?

Unfortunately, it seems thoses files are erroneous. As I said, stm32h747IG has only 1M flash (512 HB per bank).
I submitted an internal ticket to change FLASH_SIZE definition.
And so h7 family is impacted by potential discontinuity.
As FLASH_SIZE (as well as FLASH_BANK_SIZE) is not reliable for now, you can use `LL_GetFlashSize()`

> Unfortunately, it seems thoses files are erroneous. As I said, stm32h747IG has only 1M flash (512 HB per bank).

Ok, my bad.

~I'll look into it then. How can I test my code on this particular chip ?~
